findings.fix: Create the missing ConfigMap "billing-config" in namespace billing with the keys the app expects (or remove the envFrom reference if it is not needed), then let the ReplicaSet recreate the pod.

diagnosis.summary: billing pod billing-597d6775c9-ht8g5 is stuck in CreateContainerConfigError: its spec pulls env from ConfigMap \"billing-config\", which does not exist in the billing namespace (only kube-root-ca.crt is present). The Deployment billing must be fixed by creating that ConfigMap (or dropping the envFrom reference); the pod is the victim.

findings.name: orders-api
findings.root_cause: orders-api crashes at startup with 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set' (exit 1) because the Deployment's container defines no env vars or envFrom, so the required database configuration is never provided; the pod restart-loops and the orders page has no backend.
findings.fix: Add DATABASE_URL to the orders-api container via env/envFrom in the Deployment (from a Secret or ConfigMap holding the database connection string), then redeploy.

diagnosis.summary: orders/orders-api crash-loops (5 restarts, exit code 1): its logs end in 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set', and the pod spec shows no env vars or envFrom — the Deployment simply never provides the required database configuration. No other objects in the namespace are involved; the fix is to supply DATABASE_URL (e.g. from a Secret/ConfigMap) in the Deployment's container spec."

findings.name: stock-db
findings.root_cause: stock-db's container is OOMKilled (exit 137) because its 24Mi memory limit is too small for the 'loading stock index into memory' phase; the DB pod never becomes ready, so stock-api cannot reach stock-db:5432 and crash-loops.
findings.fix: Raise the stock-db Deployment memory request/limit well above 24Mi (e.g. 256Mi or more) so the in-memory stock-index load survives, then restart the deployment.

diagnosis.summary: stock-api crash-loops because it cannot connect to stock-db:5432. The real failure is upstream: the stock-db pod is repeatedly OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts, BackOff events) — its 24Mi memory limit is exceeded when the container loads the stock index into memory, so the DB never becomes ready and stock-api exits with 'stock-db:5432 unreachable'. Root cause object: the stock-db Deployment's memory limit. Fix: raise stock-db's memory request/limit (e.g. 256Mi+) so the index load completes.

Root cause object: Deployment/thumbnailer (log-shipper spec). Fix: restore the collector connection and/or raise the ephemeral-storage limit or cap the buffer.

findings.fix: Point the Service selector at the real workload, e.g. app=ledger-api (or add that label to the intended gateway pods).

diagnosis.summary: Two independent faults in namespace ledger: (1) Deployment ledger crash-loops — its container exits 2 with 'panic: invalid config key \"retries\": expected integer, got \"three\"', i.e. bad app config; (2) Service ledger-api has selector app=ledger-gateway which matches no pods (actual labels are app=ledger / app=ledger-api), so it has zero endpoints and does not answer. The ledger-api deployment itself is healthy (1/1 ready). No TLS, quota or scheduling issues involved."

findings.name: report-worker
findings.root_cause: Container is OOMKilled (exit 137) seconds after start because its memory limit of 32Mi is too small for the workload; the kernel kills it before any error is written to stdout, which is why the logs show no error.
findings.fix: Raise the report-worker container's memory limit above its working set (e.g. 128Mi, with a matching request), or reduce the cache size it warms at startup.

diagnosis.summary: report-worker in namespace reports crash-loops: every instance is OOMKilled (exit code 137) shortly after start against a 32Mi memory limit, and the BackOff events explain the restarts. The process dies from the kernel OOM killer before logging anything, matching 'no error in its logs'. Root cause is the undersized memory limit on the Deployment's container spec.

findings.name: cache
findings.root_cause: The cache pod requests nodeSelector disktype=nvme, but the only node (doctor-lab-control-plane) is labeled disktype=standard, so the scheduler reports 0/1 nodes available and the pod stays Pending forever.
findings.fix: Remove or correct the nodeSelector on the cache Deployment (the cluster's only node has disktype=standard, not nvme), or add an nvme-labeled node; then the pod will schedule.

diagnosis.summary: The cache deployment's single pod is stuck Pending: it carries nodeSelector disktype=nvme while the cluster's only node doctor-lab-control-plane is labeled disktype=standard. The scheduler fails with 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', so no replica ever runs. Fix is to change the nodeSelector in the cache Deployment spec (or provision a matching node).

findings.name: ml-trainer
findings.root_cause: ml-trainer's pod requests 64 CPUs (1Gi memory), but the cluster's single node has only 2 CPUs; no other pods are consuming CPU, so the request alone makes the pod unschedulable and it stays Pending.
findings.fix: Lower the ml-trainer container CPU request to fit the node (e.g. 1–2 CPUs) or add a node with enough CPU capacity.

diagnosis.summary: ml-trainer has been Pending because its pod requests 64 CPUs while the cluster's only node has 2 CPUs. Scheduler event 'Insufficient cpu' confirms this; no other pods in the namespace are using CPU. Fix: reduce the Deployment's CPU request to fit the node (or add capacity).

findings.name: team-quota
findings.root_cause: renderer scaled to 5 but only 2 pods exist: the namespace ResourceQuota team-quota caps pods at 2 (used 2/2), so pod creation for replicas 3-5 is rejected with 'exceeded quota: team-quota'.
findings.fix: Raise the pods limit in ResourceQuota team-quota (e.g. kubectl patch resourcequota team-quota -n batch -p '{"spec":{"hard":{"pods":"5"}}}') or remove the pods cap if not needed.

diagnosis.summary: renderer Deployment in batch wants 5 replicas but only 2 are running because ResourceQuota team-quota limits the namespace to 2 pods and is fully used. Pod creation fails with FailedCreate 'exceeded quota'. Fix is on the quota, not the deployment.

findings.name: pricing-api
findings.root_cause: Calls to the pricing-api Service fail with connection refused because the Service forwards port 80 to targetPort 8080, but the pricing-api container listens on containerPort 80; nothing listens on 8080 in the pod, so every proxied connection is refused even though the pod is Ready.
findings.fix: Change the Service port targetPort from 8080 to 80 to match the container's listening port (or set the containerPort to 8080 if the app should listen there).

diagnosis.summary: pricing-api pods are healthy and ready (nginx listening on containerPort 80), but the pricing-api Service maps port 80 -> targetPort 8080, which no process in the pod listens on. Result: kube-proxy forwards traffic to a dead port and clients (e.g. the traffic probe pod) get 'Connection refused' against the Service ClusterIP 10.96.163.4. Fix is a one-line change to the Service spec: targetPort 80.

findings.name: web
findings.root_cause: nginx in the web container listens on its default port 80, but the deployment's readiness probe does HTTP GET / on port 8081, which nothing serves; every probe gets connection refused, so the pod stays NotReady (0/1) and gets no traffic despite the container running fine.
findings.fix: Change the readiness probe in the web Deployment to target port 80 (where nginx listens), or set NGINX_PORT/listen directive to 8081 if 8081 is the intended port.

diagnosis.summary: web/web-7969d6cc4c-46fdj runs nginx (started cleanly per logs) but the Deployment's readiness probe hits http://pod:8081/, while nginx listens on 80 — repeated 'connection refused' readiness failures keep the pod at 0/1 ready, so it receives no traffic. Fix: point the readiness probe at port 80 (or make nginx listen on 8081). No Service exists in the namespace, but the reported symptom is fully explained by the probe/port mismatch.

findings.name: catalog
findings.root_cause: Hotfix set image nginx:1.29-alpine-hotfix on Deployment catalog; tag not found in docker.io (ErrImagePull), so the new pod is stuck in ImagePullBackOff and the rollout hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded while old pods keep serving.
findings.fix: Publish the hotfix image under a valid tag (or correct the tag/registry in the Deployment) and re-trigger the rollout; alternatively roll back to the previous revision until the image is available.

diagnosis.summary: Catalog hotfix deploy rolled out image nginx:1.29-alpine-hotfix, which does not exist in docker.io (ErrImagePull NotFound). New pod catalog-58664cc6f-bhmp9 is in ImagePullBackOff; Deployment catalog shows Progressing=False/ProgressDeadlineExceeded with only 1 of 2 desired replicas updated. Old ReplicaSet pods remain ready and serving, explaining why users still see the old version. Fix: use a valid hotfix image tag (or roll back).

findings.name: auth-api-cert
findings.root_cause: session-svc proxies /login to https://auth-api whose server cert (CN auth-api) expired 2026-09-26; nginx rejects the upstream handshake with 'certificate has expired' and returns 502 for every login.

diagnosis.summary: Logins fail with 502 through session-svc because its nginx verifies upstream https://auth-api against the internal CA, and the auth-api leaf cert (ConfigMap auth-api-cert) expired 2026-09-26. Nginx logs show repeated 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)' on GET /login returning 502. The issuing CA is valid until 2036, so only the leaf needs reissuing. No deployments today, consistent with time-based expiry."

findings.root_cause: Liveness probe runs a 300000-iteration busy loop before its wget check with timeoutSeconds=1, while the container has a 10m CPU limit; throttled, the loop can't finish in time, so the probe always times out and kubelet kills the healthy nginx (exit 0).

rejected_submission.summary: search-web restarts with no app errors because its liveness probe is broken: it runs a 300000-iteration busy loop before its wget check, with timeoutSeconds=1, while the container CPU limit is only 10m. Throttled at the limit, the loop can't finish within 1s, so the probe always times out ('command timed out after 1s'); kubelet kills the otherwise healthy nginx (clean logs, SIGQUIT, exit 0) → CrashLoopBackOff. Fix on the search-web Deployment: simplify the probe to the wget check, increase its timeout, and/or raise the CPU limit.

findings.name: orders-api
findings.root_cause: orders-api pod crash-loops (exit 1, BackOff) because the container logs 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set' — the Deployment defines no env or envFrom at all, so the required database configuration was never provided.
findings.fix: Add the missing database configuration to the orders-api Deployment (set DATABASE_URL via an env entry or a Secret/ConfigMap referenced through envFrom), then roll out.

findings.name: checkout
findings.root_cause: Service checkout selects app=checkout-v2 but the only pods in the namespace carry app=checkout (from Deployment checkout), so the selector matches 0 pods and the service has no ready endpoints.
findings.fix: Align the selector: change Service checkout's selector to app=checkout (or label the checkout Deployment's pods with app=checkout-v2).

diagnosis.summary: Audited orders, status, checkout. orders: orders-api crash-loops with exit 1 because DATABASE_URL is never configured (no env/envFrom on the Deployment) — root cause config_missing. checkout: Service 'checkout' selector app=checkout-v2 matches no pods (pods are labeled app=checkout), leaving it with zero endpoints. status: healthy — status-page 1/1 ready, service selector matches its pod, no problem pods or warnings.

findings.fix: Point checkout-web's trust volume at the internal-ca ConfigMap (or add the Internal Services CA 2026 cert to the mounted bundle) instead of legacy-ca, then roll the deployment.
findings.name: checkout-web
findings.root_cause: After the payments migration, payments-api serves a cert issued by 'Internal Services CA 2026', but checkout-web verifies upstreams against legacy-ca ('Legacy Services CA 2021'), so nginx fails the upstream handshake and returns 502 on /pay; payments-api itself is healthy.

diagnosis.summary: payments-api is NOT down: 1/1 ready with a ready endpoint on 443. The 502s come from checkout-web: nginx logs show repeated 'upstream SSL certificate verify error (21)' when proxying /pay to https://payments-api:443. checkout-web mounts its CA trust from ConfigMap legacy-ca (only 'Legacy Services CA 2021'); internal-ca ('Internal Services CA 2026', valid since 2026-09-26, matching this morning's migration) is the issuer of the new payments-api cert. Fix: make checkout-web trust internal-ca.
